import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load the dataset
coffee_sales = pd.read_csv('data/coffee_sales.csv')

# Create a new column for total sales per product
coffee_sales['total_sales'] = coffee_sales['price'] * coffee_sales['quantity']

# Set the aesthetics for the plot
sns.set(style='whitegrid')

# Create a bar plot for total sales by product
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))
sales_by_product = coffee_sales.groupby('product')['total_sales'].sum().reset_index()
sns.barplot(x='total_sales', y='product', data=sales_by_product, palette='viridis')

# Add titles and labels
plt.title('Total Sales by Coffee Product', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Total Sales ($)', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Product', fontsize=12)

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load the dataset
coffee_sales = pd.read_csv('data/coffee_sales.csv')

# Create a new column for total sales per product
coffee_sales['total_sales'] = coffee_sales['price'] * coffee_sales['quantity']

# Set the aesthetics for the plot
sns.set(style='whitegrid')

# Create a bar plot for total sales by product
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))
sales_by_product = coffee_sales.groupby('product')['total_sales'].sum().reset_index()
sns.barplot(x='total_sales', y='product', data=sales_by_product, palette='viridis')

# Add titles and labels
plt.title('Total Sales by Coffee Product', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Total Sales ($)', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Product', fontsize=12)

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
